items.title: Consan compile of a tcgen05 kernel for sm_120a aborts the process (LLVM ERROR: Cannot select tcgen05.wait.st)
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Compiling a Gluon kernel that uses tcgen05 for sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000) fails two different ways depending on `TRITON_INSTRUMENTATION_MODE`:

- without consan, ptxas rejects the PTX and Python gets a clean `PTXASError` ("Instruction 'tcgen05.alloc' not supported on .target 'sm_120a'");
- with `TRITON_INSTRUMENTATION_MODE=consan`, the process aborts before ptxas:

```
LLVM ERROR: Cannot select: intrinsic %llvm.nvvm.tcgen05.wait.st
```

exit code 134. Under pytest the abort kills the xdist worker, and every test scheduled on it fails with `BrokenPipeError` or `child process exited with code -6`, which is how `python/test/gluon/test_consan.py` shows 300 failures on sm_120 (gating for that in #11746). The kernel can never run on sm_120, so the point is only that a fatal error is the wrong way to say so: a verifier or lowering error on the tcgen05 ops for a target without `supportsTcgen05` would keep the process alive, and the instrumentation pass could skip its `tcgen05.wait::st` on such a target.

### Reproducer

`main` at 972d18aa0, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), CUDA 12.8 driver:

```python
import os, sys, torch
sys.path.insert(0, "python/test/gluon")
os.environ["TRITON_INSTRUMENTATION_MODE"] = "consan"  # drop this line for the clean PTXASError
from triton import knobs
knobs.refresh_knobs()
import test_consan as tc
K, BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K = 512, tc.mma_block_m(1), tc.mma_block_n(1), 64
A = torch.randn((BLOCK_M, K), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
tc.load_local_alloc_mma_write_after_read_kernel[(1,)](A, K, BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K, num_ctas=1)
```

### Environment details

Triton `main` 972d18aa0 built from source, torch 2.11.0+cu128, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (sm_120).

items.title: 3.8.0 lacks eleven fixes that main's own tests catch on the wheel (wrong results, a device fault, crashes); cherry-picks built and verified
items.body:
This is a follow-up to #11730 and #11733, with the method turned around: instead of running the release's tests on the wheel, I ran main's `python/test/unit/language` tests (main at 42c5e89c3) against the 3.8.0 wheel on an RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120), one process per failing test, and kept the failures whose test was added by a fix and whose symptom a user of the wheel can hit through the public API. `release/3.8.x` is one commit above its merge base with main (3bb23dde7, 23 Jun), so every fix below is simply absent from 3.8.0. All of these reproduce on the pure wheel; the ones marked with a cherry-pick apply to `release/3.8.x` without conflicts; I built the branch with all of them (on top of #11731 and #11734) on the same board and main's tests for each pass there.

Wrong results:

- `tl.dot_scaled` with an E8M0 scale byte of 0 or a scale that is subnormal in bf16: every element wrong (`test_scaled_dot_minimum_scale`, `test_scaled_dot_zero_scale`, 16384 of 16384 elements). Fixed by #11624 (10 Sep); the core part (`DecomposeScaledBlocked`, the interpreter, `tools/mxfp.py`, plus the AMD caller of the changed helper) applies with a 3-way merge and passes the whole `test_scaled_dot` family (1728 cases) on the board; the AMD upcast, fpsan and triton_kernels parts are separate.
- `OptimizeThreadLocality` reorders a reduction incorrectly: `test_optimize_thread_locality_preserves_rows`, 256 of 256 elements wrong. Fixed by #11186 (5 Aug), clean cherry-pick.
- `tl.range(..., flatten=True)` with an inner loop that can be empty: the flattened loop drops iterations (`test_tl_range_fuse_empty_inner_bounds`, 352 instead of 337). Fixed by #11607 and its reland #11688 (10 Sep); #11607 is clean, #11688 conflicts only in the lit file.
- `tl.softmax` normalizes along the wrong axis for `dim != -1` (`test_softmax`, 4 of 4 elements). Fixed by #11409 (24 Aug), clean.
- A list comprehension with an `if` filter in a `constexpr` context ignores the filter: `[x for x in (10, 20, 30, 40) if x >= 30]` has four elements on the wheel, two on main (`test_list_comprehension_if_filter`). Fixed by #10888 (15 Jul), clean.
- `tl.full(shape, -0.0, tl.float32)` produces +0.0 on the wheel (sign bit clear), -0.0 on main (`test_scalar_constant_preserves_signed_zero`). Fixed by #11426 (24 Aug), clean.

Crashes and device faults:

- A pipelined TMA load whose stage size is not 16-byte aligned faults on the device: `test_tma_load_unaligned_stage_size` ends in `CUDA error: misaligned address`, and the error is sticky for the process. Fixed by #10898 (17 Jul), clean cherry-pick (7 files).
- `tl.gather` with a [4096, 4] index tensor over a [4, 4] source: `PassManager::run failed` (`test_gather[src_shape2-indices_shape2-0]`). This is the class of #11600; fixed by #10838 (13 Jul), clean.
- `tl.dot_scaled` with an unscaled bf16 lhs and an MN-packed fp4 rhs: `PassManager::run failed` (`test_dot_scaled_unscaled_lhs_fp4_rhs`). Fixed by #11613 (6 Sep), clean.
- A `while` loop whose condition is an integer rather than a bool: `error encountered during parsing` (`test_while_integer_condition`). Fixed by #11234 (19 Aug), clean.
- `tl.histogram` on a non-32-bit input fails inside the pass manager instead of with a frontend error (`test_err_histogram_non_32bit_int`). #10891 (9 Aug), clean.

Not included, for the record: the rest of the 443 failures are new APIs (`atomic_poll`, `atomic_load/store`, CLC, keyword-only arguments, `topk` checks, tuple targets in comprehensions), the BC-breaking promotion changes (#11472, #11473, #10883), and test-side changes.

I can open the cherry-pick PRs the same way as #11731 and #11734 if a 3.8.1 is on the table; the device fault and the dot_scaled results would be my first two.

items.title: 3.8.0 on sm_120: MN-packed mxfp4 dot_scaled returns wrong results and batched scaled dots fail an assert; both fixed on main (#10726, #11262)
items.body:
Running the `release/3.8.x` tests against the 3.8.0 wheel on an RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120, CUDA 12.8 torch build) turns up two more sm_120 problems that main fixed after the branch point, next to #11730.

`test_matmul.py::test_block_scale_fp4` with `mxfp4` and `pack_along_k=False` compiles and runs, and every element of the result is wrong: the six configurations with `BLOCK_M >= 128` fail `assert_close` with 524214 of 524288 elements off (greatest absolute difference 188.4 against a reference in the tens). #10726 routes the MN-packed FP4 case to the decomposition path on SM120; its description says the codegen crashed, on 3.8.0 it does not crash, it returns garbage. An independent executable-semantics check of the same kernels agrees with the test's reference, not with the device.

`test_matmul.py::test_batched_mxfp`, all 36 cases, fail with `PassManager::run failed` after `LinearLayoutConversions.cpp:1451: combineCtaCgaWithShape: Assertion 'ctaLayout.getNumOutDims() == rank' failed`. #11262 generalizes the SM120 scaled-dot scale layout to rank 3.

Both cherry-pick cleanly onto `release/3.8.x` (+36/-2 and +53/-17), and #11257 brings the test limits for SM12 (+9/-3). I've built the branch with them on the same board: `test_block_scale_fp4` mxfp4 goes from 6 wrong-result failures to all `assert_close` passing (the only leftovers are the release test's own `kind::mxf8f6f4` PTX assertion, which #11257 gates for the fallback), and `test_batched_mxfp` from 36 pass failures to 30 passed and 6 skipped for shared memory. If a 3.8.1 is on the table I'll open the PR the same way as #11731.
